arc: Vic asked his daughter to marry in the morning and she asked what time kick-off was, which nobody can tell her; the six tickets cannot leave his phone and he cannot leave the wedding, so the phone has to travel without him, and after seventy-five days of typing Danny sends four words: "Leave it with me." (Episode 5). The airline then needs a surname for every seat and, after eleven years, nobody in the chat has Danny's: he is "Danny Football" in every phone, and the one person who knows it is not in the chat (Short A). Maya booked seven seats and four people fly, in T-shirts that are right for one day: Vic is at a wedding, Lee found it cheaper (three flights and a bus, arriving "before kick-off, depending on kick-off"), Danny has no surname, and the phone with the six tickets is in a floral armchair, because Danny left it with his grandmother, who does not answer a phone that is not hers (Episode 6). The day before, the kick-off time is confirmed at last, in green, and moved within three seconds for television, to a time that suits only Sydney, who is not going, and that turns Lee's route into an arrival at half-time (Short B). On match day the four who did everything properly are at the gate and learn where their tickets are from Sydney, who has seen Danny's grandmother on television: she is in her seat, early, with Vic's phone ringing in her hand ("That'll be for Vic."), Danny is behind her, and Vic is recorded as attending his twelfth match from his daughter's wedding (Episode 7). The season ends where the last one did, at greater expense and with everyone content: two got in, one is not in the chat and the other is typing, and the study stamps it CONFIRMED on the same kind of frozen frame that was stamped TO BE CONFIRMED in Episode 1; Lee arrives at half-time having missed nothing, on Friday Vic pays and OWE MAYA moves for the first time, to 5, Danny at last answers the question the chat is named after ("I'm in.") and stops typing, Jo's verdict is "It was fine.", the grandmother's status is WENT., and the last line is "Next season: to be confirmed."

why:
The spine is Writer A's, because it is the one where the grandmother stays one step ahead without trying and the season closes on its own premise. The phone goes to Danny, Danny leaves it with his grandmother, and the tickets go in without the people who planned. The finale replays Episode 1's "Two arrived. Neither was in the chat." one notch drier and stamps it CONFIRMED on the same kind of frozen frame. Writer B's finale had Danny inside on a ticket nobody could account for; in this one the count closes (six tickets, six travelling once Vic is out, Danny uses one, the grandmother has her paper one).

What I took from Writer B, where it was sharper:
- Vic's cold open, put into direct speech so the first line is six words. The bride's "what time's kick-off?" is the question from "It's Pinned" asked a fifteenth time, and the board's heading answers it in the cut.
- "Danny Football", the most recognisable observation in either script. It is re-motivated (the airline needs a surname for every seat) and made to matter: NO SURNAME is why Danny is not on the flight two days later.
- The T-shirts being right for one day.
- Lee's "Three flights and a bus. I get in before kick-off, depending on kick-off." and "Lee lives forty minutes from the airport."
- The unseen daughter as a three-step runner: "I did ask her", then "what time's kick-off?", then "My daughter says I didn't look at my phone once."
- Vic's record ticking from 11 to 12 while he is at the wedding.
- "I'm in." as the message that ends the typing, sent on the Friday under the chat's own name.

What I cut:
- A's opener, which repeated Episode 4's last line.
- A's separate short for the grandmother and the phone. In A a follower learned it on Tuesday and was told again on Thursday; here it happens once, as Episode 6's top, spoken by her.
- A third use of Maya's closed eyes.
- Jo typing "Should be fine." again, which would have made it a catchphrase. It survives as her name tag and pays off as "It was fine."
- B's on-screen Danny and "Both are Danny" (a new face, and a joke that needs a second look).
- B's "Leave what with you?" and "I don't know what 'it' is" (they explain the joke).
- B's cascade of "Paid." (Vic paying on a Friday and the chip moving by one is drier).
- The second "seventy-five days" line.
- The struck-through pinned time, which the pinned bar cannot draw.

Threads paid: Danny's typing, the tickets on Vic's phone, the wedding, Vic's record, Jo, OWE MAYA and "which Friday", Lee, Sydney (the answer comes from Sydney again), the kick-off time ("7:45 or 8": it was 8, for three seconds), the Saturday T-shirts, the grandmother's ticket, the series title. The Elsewhere man is left as closed by his own ARRIVED stamp.

Limits:
- Narration is 272 characters of 700, in seven lines (300 if the fallback line is needed).

If "Nothing." or "It was fine." is played with any self-pity, or Danny reads as having abandoned them, the ending turns sour and Maya becomes the fool the bible forbids. It needs flat performances and every silence held.
